sources.title: Baisha Village, Baisha Ancient Town, Lijiang - GoGrandChina
sources.content:
Baisha Village Content Extraction

Location & Overview
Baisha Village is positioned "10 km from the Old Town of Lijiang" and comprises part of the World Heritage "Old Town of Lijiang" designation. The settlement sits "on the foot of the Yulong Snow Mountain."

Historical Significance
The ancient town "was the political, commercial and cultural center for the local Naxi people" spanning "400 years from the year 658 AD to 1107 AD." It functioned as "the center of silk embroidery in the southwest of China" and served as "the most important place of the Ancient Southern Silk Road."

Key Attractions
Dabaoji Palace & Frescoes: Built in 658 AD during the Tang Dynasty, featuring "55 still in existence" religious artworks painted by "Han, Naxi, Tibetan and Bai ethnic minorities" depicting "Buddhism, Tibetan Buddhism and Taoism."

Naxi Architecture: The village preserves "many complete Naxi architectures and cultural sites."

Mu Family Heritage: Described as "the hometown of Mu family, the first family of Lijiang."

Practical Information
- Best visiting period: April to October
- Duration: 2-3 hours recommended
- Access fee: Free general entry; CNY 30 for Baisha Frescoes
- Hours: Open all day
- Transportation: Bus 6 from Lijiang Old Town or private car rental available

Visitor Guidelines
Recommendations include wearing "sunscreen, hat and sunglasses" and retaining "the entrance ticket of the Lijiang Old Town" for verification when visiting frescoes. Photography restrictions prohibit "flash" use to protect artifacts.

sources.title: Quick Travel Guide to Baisha Old Town in Lijiang - Fabio Nodari
sources.content:
Quick Travel Guide to Baisha Old Town in Lijiang

Baisha (白沙) is a small ancient town just 20 minutes from the more famous Lijiang Old Town. As the oldest and most original Naxi village, Baisha Old Town is not only the cradle-land of Mu Family but also the earliest settlement of Naxi people.

Located about 12 kilometers north of Lijiang City, it's still somehow underrated and not overcrowded, although recently it has seen an increase in tourists.

Transportation: You can bike there, take a bus (No. 6), or take a taxi. By car, it shouldn't take longer than 20 minutes. Use Didi or similar apps to call a driver if taxis are scarce.

Best Time to Visit: October to November (clear autumn air, clearer snow mountain views), March to April (cherry blossoms bloom, fewer people). Avoid peak travel seasons during winter and summer holidays.

Main Attractions: There is only an old commercial street here, and there are many local Naxi courtyards, which retain the original appearance of the ancient town. You can see the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain when you look up. An exciting stop is Dabaoji Palace, where you can see an impressive collection of large mural paintings.

Entrance Fees: Ancient town is free, Baisha Murals (Wenchang Palace/Da Baoji Palace) 30 RMB per person, photography inside the halls is prohibited.

What to Do: There isn't much else to do in Baisha besides wandering through its charming alleys, stopping at one of the many excellent coffee shops, or enjoying a meal in one of the local restaurants. But that is precisely the point. People who come here are not looking for action or entertainment; they come to slow down, breathe, and enjoy the atmosphere of a village that still feels authentic.

The Naxi Embroidery Institute (白沙纳西传统手工刺绣院) is situated only a few steps north of the main market square. It was established to preserve local embroidery, which often features motifs inspired by nature.

The food has a very strong Tibetan influence because Baisha is one of the first places where the Naxi settled after migrating down from the Tibetan plateau. Visitors can sample local dishes such as yak meat pies in Tibetan restaurants.

Travel Tips: Wear sunscreen, hat and sunglasses to prevent sunburns. To protect the relics, do not touch or scribble on the frescoes. Do not use flash to take pictures.

sources.title: Baisha Village in Lijiang, China - Tiny Urban Kitchen
sources.content:
Baisha Village in Lijiang, China

Baisha is known for its ancient Naxi culture, preserved with an untouched, timeless feel - cobblestone streets, rustic wooden buildings, and people dressed in traditional clothing. It hasn't really been built up at all and it was really nice wandering up and down alleys admiring the peace and quiet, lack of costume selfie takers, and chilling in the cafes.

The village preserves authentic local life that's increasingly rare in China's ancient towns. Visitors can see traditional Naxi women in their daily activities, local craftspeople at work, and experience a slower pace of life compared to the bustling Lijiang Old Town.

sources.title: Baisha Old Town Lijiang Travel Guide - Yunnan Exploration
sources.content:
Baisha Ancient Town Lijiang Travel Guide

Baisha Ancient Town is the oldest of the three ancient towns that make up the UNESCO World Heritage Old Town of Lijiang. Located at the foot of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, about 10 kilometers north of Lijiang Old Town, Baisha was the original seat of power for the Mu clan rulers and the political center of the Naxi people.

The town preserves many complete Naxi architectural sites and cultural relics. Its most famous attraction is the collection of Baisha Murals (白沙壁画) in Dabaoji Palace, dating from the Ming Dynasty.

Key highlights include the ancient commercial street, traditional Naxi courtyard homes, and stunning views of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. The town offers a much more authentic and peaceful experience compared to the busier Lijiang and Shuhe ancient towns.

sources.title: Exploring Lijiang's countryside: A day-trip to Baisha - GoKunming
sources.content:
Exploring Lijiang's countryside: A day-trip to Baisha

Baisha is the oldest of the three Naxi ancient towns near Lijiang, and the birthplace of the Mu clan. Unlike the heavily commercialized Lijiang Old Town, Baisha retains much of its original character with local families still living traditional lifestyles.

The town's most significant cultural attraction is the Baisha Murals (白沙壁画), a collection of religious frescoes spanning several temples including Dabaoji Palace and Liuli Hall. These murals uniquely blend Buddhist, Taoist, and Lamaist imagery in a single composition - a rarity in Chinese art.

Visitors can explore the main commercial street, visit local artisan workshops, sample traditional Naxi food, and enjoy unobstructed views of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. The town is easily reached by bus No. 6 from Lijiang Old Town.

sources.title: 白沙古镇（云南省丽江市境内旅游景区）- 百度百科
sources.content:
白沙古镇文字内容提取

基本信息
白沙古镇位于云南省丽江市玉龙纳西族自治县白沙镇，距丽江古城北约10公里，北临玉龙雪山，南至龙泉，西依芝山。这是纳西族最早聚居地及木氏土司政权发祥地，宋元时期为丽江政治、经济、文化中心。

建筑特色
民居建筑群占地1.06平方千米，布局以南北主轴为中心，保留"三坊一照壁"传统民居格局，现存90%以上明清时期建筑风貌。

非遗文化
古镇现存白沙壁画、白沙细乐等12项国家级及省市级非物质文化遗产。壁画分布在大宝积宫、琉璃殿等庙堂，由明初至清初创作，融合多民族绘画技法。现存55幅白沙壁画，多创作于明清两朝，融会了藏传佛教绘画风格，距今已有五百年历史。

历史沿革
白沙是纳西族古都，曾为丽江政治、经济、商贸和文化中心。唐朝时，南诏王封玉龙雪山为"北岳"，木氏祖先就开始在此修建白沙街和北岳庙。宋元时期至明代初1383年，木氏家族才迁至大研镇。

主要景点

四方街：白沙古镇的四方街是束河古镇及丽江古城四方街的雏形，曾为繁华的交易集贸中心。本地老奶奶仍在此卖菜，穿着传统纳西服饰。

牌楼：四方街正南侧立有两层牌楼，上有牌匾"世界文化遗产纳西古王国之都--白沙"。

大石桥：白沙古镇的大石桥是丽江最古老的大石桥，是束河古镇青龙桥和丽江大研古镇大石桥的前身，为茶马古道马帮必经之路。

白沙壁画：大宝积宫的壁画是丽江壁画中规模最大的，绘制于明万历年间，共12幅，绘有167个人物形象。内容融合汉传佛教、道教和喇嘛教佛像，在同一幅壁画里呈现不同教派内容，十分罕见。

福国寺：坐落于白沙西边的芝山上，是纳西木氏土司的家庙。

白沙机场：白沙古镇往东5公里的荒坝是二战时期飞虎队的机场之一。

手工艺

积善铜艺：四方街旁有铜匠铺，代代相传，是非物质文化遗产传承人的手工艺坊。历史上白沙有150多家打铜作坊。

白沙锦绣艺术院：是政府重点扶持的民族刺绣及东巴文化传承、推广和妇女就业示范基地。

特色小吃

鸡豆凉粉：白沙街上有最传统的鸡豆凉粉，由特殊原生态小豆子做成，价格约5元一盒。
手工豆腐：白沙的手工豆腐也是一绝，四方街白沙时光餐厅对面有唯一一家，早上10点后通常售罄。

住宿信息
镇上大约有四十家客栈，从普通客栈到高端度假会馆都有，房间价格从几十元到上千元一晚。

交通信息
公交：从象山市场、束河北门乘6路公交车至"白沙"下车即是。
骑行：从大研古城骑自行车去白沙古镇，车程约12公里。
观光火车：丽江于2025年2月12日开通全程20.7公里的雪山观光火车线路，串联白沙古镇、玉水寨、东巴谷、甘海子等多个景点。该列车为全球首列全景观光山地旅游列车。

节庆活动
棒棒会：纳西语叫"白沙当美空普"，意为"白沙大宝积宫开门"。明代以来延续下来的传统。
火把节：农历6月24-26日，纳西族要在院子里点三个晚上的篝火。

sources.title: 丽江古城旅游攻略 - 知乎（白沙相关内容）
sources.content:
白沙古镇游玩攻略补充信息

白沙古镇是丽江三大古镇中最古老、最原始的一个，商业化程度最低。古镇不收门票，白沙壁画门票30元/人。

主要看点：白沙壁画（大宝积宫）、纳西刺绣、传统手工艺作坊、四方街集市。

建议游玩时间：2-3小时。

最佳拍照时间：清晨和傍晚，可以拍到玉龙雪山做背景的绝美照片。

美食推荐：鸡豆凉粉、手工豆腐、纳西粑粑。
